newsitem.title: CHINA: Widow of China's last emperor dies at 73.
newsitem.headline: Widow of China's last emperor dies at 73.

text.p: Li Shuxian, the widow of China's last emperor, has died of lung cancer in Beijing, the official Xinhua news agency said on Tuesday. She was 73.

Li, the second wife of Aisin Gioro Pu Yi, died on Monday, Xinhua said. Pu Yi was the last emperor of China's Qing dynasty that ended in 1911 with the founding of a republic. Li, the second wife of Aisin Gioro Pu Yi, died on Monday, Xinhua said. Pu Yi was the last emperor of China's Qing dynasty that ended in 1911 with the founding of a republic. She met Pu Yi, who was known as the Emperor Xuan Tong during his brief reign from 1908 to 1911, when she was a nurse while he was in hospital after the 1949 communist takeover. The two married and set up house together in 1962, Pu Yi said in his autobiography. The couple had no children.

Li led a quiet life, virtually retiring from public view after Pu Yi died in 1967. She appeared briefly in April 1995 to bury the ashes of her late husband in a new graveyard among the huge tombs of his imperial ancestors on the outskirts of Beijing.
